choices.why: A light ash-grey three-seater about 2 m wide, with a tailored line and raised tapered legs, so it reads light against the long white wall.
A 170x240 light grey flatweave with fine black stripes that frames the seating area and echoes the black balcony frame.
Pale blond ash with slim splayed legs, giving exactly the light wood look the user asked for without crowding the room.
A long, low off-white console on slim legs that keeps the bright, airy feel opposite the sofa.
A white drum shade on a slim brushed-steel stem gives soft, elegant light beside the sofa and takes almost no visual space.
Textured mustard cushions add warm colour against the light grey sofa.
A tall, airy areca palm that brings fresh green to the balcony end of the room.
White semi-sheer panels soften the daylight while keeping the room bright and the balcony view open.

answer.why: Light grey, white and pale ash keep the room bright and modern on its grey-wood floor. Mustard cushions and a green palm add colour, and the thin black stripes in the rug tie in with the black balcony frame.
